title: Bodybuilding in a Nutshell
author: Teoman Bedel
desc: You should crush every single rep and set to meaningfully progress through this program. If you focus on correcting your form and picking a efficient tempo, you’ll quickly realize that one to two sets are actually enough volume for “most” of the time.

ex.note: If you don’t feel comfortable with a regular chest press machine, you can swap it with any flat pressing exercise that focuses mainly on chest. Barbell bench press is not recommended.
Same logic here; pick any incline fly exercise that suits you.
This is your main upper back exercise in this program, so you should prioritize pulling the attachment toward your chest while leaning your torso back slightly.
Ah, the king of the ego-lifting exercises. Forget your ego and focus on your form and tempo to see how amazing this exercise actually is. Keep your torso still and pull down with your elbows.
Nothing fancy here, yet you should focus on pulling down your elbow to actually peform the exercise with an efficient form. Using a bench to provide chest support is highly recommended.
Raise your arms as high as possible without breaking the form.

ex.n: Single Arm Rear Delt Cable Fly
ex.note: This one can be tricky, so you should prioritize finding your own sweet spot before anything else.
Single arm works better here as you can keep your arm as straight as possible, which creates an overall better tension at the target muscle.
Rope, cable, cuff, sitting, standing; whatever you want. Anything that’s overhead works here.
Keep your body still, squeeze your butt and lift only with your hamstrings. Imagine curling with your bicep, since they’re incredibly similar. Trust me, it works.
God I love this exercise; but only if you do it correctly. Keep the back seat as far back as possible to find the sweet spot for your knees to “extend”, duh.
When your body leans forward during squats, it heavily shifts the focus from your quads to your glutes, hence that’s why we go smith machine here. Keep your torso upwards and work them knees.
Barbell works too, but I personally prefer dumbbells; its up to you. Focus on pushing your butt out as far as possible without breaking the tension in your hamstrings, then just lift back up.
Boring, but essential if your calfs are as weak as a chicken’s legs.
Don’t use a narrow grip handle, please. Find an attachment that mimics the grip of a regular lat pulldown, hold it wide and just lift.
Pull your elbows back and work them lats, simple as that.
Same rules, different attachment. Kill your ego.
Wider you grip the handles, more you work your chest, keep that in mind.
Simple, boring, essential. Just don’t kill your shoulders.
Don’t swing your arms like crazy, don’t raise them too high, squeeze your butt tight and try to hold the dumbbells at the top for a bit, simple as that.
Keep your arms as straight as possible while performing, otherwise, you are not working your rear delts at all.
Big guy here. This exercise depends heavily on form practicing, yet its an essential one to grow them triceps.
Don’t just push it down, also push it slightly sideways. Keep your body parallel to the handle and push like you’re pulling the pin of a grenade.
You should adjust the hand attachment to a height where you can comfortably grip it with your hand when your arm is fully extended downward. Move away from the machine, look the other way, and curl.
Yeah…
Keep your torso and butt still and only curl with your hamstrings, otherwise you are dancing rather than working your legs.
Full range of motion is the KEY. Warm your ankles good before this one, since a flexible ankle means more extension on the knees, means more emphasis on your quads. Poetic.
